properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 9:52PM MDT until July 29 at 11:30PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
At 952 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Southern Elk Burn Area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
Southern Elk Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and downstream of the Southern Elk Burn
Area.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Sheridan County.
properties.instruction:
Life threatening flooding of creeks, roads, and normally dry coulees
in and downstream of the Southern Elk burn area is likely. In
addition to the flash flooding, the heavy rains may trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding of creeks, streams, and normally dry
coulees even in areas not receiving rainfall downstream of the burn
area. These can become raging killer currents in a matter of minutes
even from distant rainfall upstream.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency officials and
request they pass the information to the National Weather Service in
Billings.

properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 200 AM MDT.

* At 807 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported flash flooding in
Lick Wash downstream through Buckskin Gulch. Between 1 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen upstream with a very large flood wave
overflowing its banks while moving south past the intersection
with US-89 heading towards Buckskin Gulch. Expect the very large
flood wave to take roughly 5 hours to reach the confluence with
the Paria River on the Utah side just north of the Arizona border.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams,
slot canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lick Wash Slot Canyon down to Buckskin Gulch in Central Kane County
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is actively occurring. It is important to know where you
are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become killers
in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or creeks.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Albany and Schenectady Counties in eastern New York.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. It will
take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 754 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicates that between 2 and 6
inches of rain have fallen. Flooding is ongoing in the warned
area.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Albany, Schenectady, Rotterdam, Scotia, Delmar, Duanesburg,
Westerlo, Ravena, Voorheesville, Altamont, Feura Bush,
Selkirk, East Glenville, New Scotland, Coeymans, Princetown,
Clarksville, New Salem, Wolf Hill and Thatcher State Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 29 at 7:23PM EDT until July 30 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New York, including the
following counties, Columbia, Greene and Ulster.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations remains ongoing. Numerous roads remain
closed due to flooding. It will take several hours for all the
water from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 721 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicates that between 5 and 9
inches of rain has fallen in the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing and expected to continue into tonight.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area through tonight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hudson, Catskill, Saugerties, New Baltimore, Coxsackie,
Athens, Saugerties South, Cairo, Veteran, Stuyvesant,
Germantown, Centerville, Leeds, Jefferson Heights,
Cauterskill, South Cairo, Cairo Junction, Hamburg Light,
Limestreet and Kiskatom.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Columbia, NY; Greene, NY; Ulster, NY

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 29 at 5:19PM EDT until July 30 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New York, including the
following counties, Columbia, Greene and Rensselaer.

* WHEN...Until 515 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 519 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area.
Between 5 and 11 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Troy, East Greenbush, Rensselaer, Hudson, Chatham, Nassau,
Claverack, New Baltimore, Coxsackie, Valatie, Athens,
Castleton-On-Hudson, Philmont, Kinderhook, Lorenz Park,
Claverack-Red Mills, West Sand Lake, Averill Park,
Wynantskill and Wyantskill.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Columbia, NY; Greene, NY; Rensselaer, NY

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 10:40AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Friday July 31.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
